open_points.subject: deliverer_router authorization responsibility
open_points.text: any check other than the request forms it reads by their models, or any delivery rule;
open_points.question: How can `deliverer_router` own “the reading of the single `Authorization` field in the Bearer scheme” when it must not own any check other than request-form checks; specifically, which module checks field multiplicity, scheme spelling and case, the single space, and token presence before identifiers and the body?
options: `deliverer_router` owns all structural Authorization checks and the prohibition is narrowed to allow them; `deliverer_api` only compares the extracted token
`deliverer_api` owns every Authorization check, while `deliverer_router` only transports the raw field through an extractor
`http_router_backend` owns structural Authorization validation and reports an extracted token or authentication failure to `deliverer_router`
open_points.default_guess: Let `deliverer_router` own the structural Authorization checks and explicitly exempt them from its Must not own rule; let `deliverer_api` own only constant-time comparison with the expected token.

witness.initial: A request has one `Authorization: Basic x` field and also has a malformed project identifier and body.
events: The router's emitted extractor reads the Authorization field before identifier and body processing.
outcomes: Following the Owns passage, `deliverer_router` checks the scheme, refuses the request as unauthorized, and the caller receives UNAUTHORIZED.
Following the Must not own passage, `deliverer_router` performs no Authorization check; identifier or body validation may refuse the request as INVALID_REQUEST before any module rejects the scheme.
